metadata.title: Claude, Closing Checklist.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude applies its own legal judgment to build a closing checklist, or follows a written instruction file, using the closing-checklist skill's own folder/SKILL.md/Steps structure as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that the skill runs the steps written in its SKILL.md, the same way every time -- not legal judgment, and nothing the file doesn't say.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B03 (a step not written in the SKILL.md's Steps section stays a dashed, unconnected card; asking for it doesn't make it run)

beats.narration_text: Here's the assumption everyone brings in: Claude just knows how to build a legal closing checklist, out of its own judgment. It doesn't. It reads one file, top to bottom, and runs what's written there. So the real question isn't what Claude knows — it's what the file tells it to do.

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it acts. Here's what's actually inside closing-checklist: one file, called SKILL.md, holding the whole instruction set in plain language. No hidden logic, no separate config, no runtime magic. The file is the program — you can open it and read exactly what Claude is about to do, in the same words Claude is reading.

shot.new_visual_element: A folder icon labelled closing-checklist/, one file card SKILL.md inside it

production_viz.label: A skill is a folder
production_viz.mechanic: A folder icon labelled 'closing-checklist/' draws in on cream. Inside it, a single file card, 'SKILL.md', fades in with a small accent border -- one file total. The folder and file hold still while a caption lands beneath: 'the file is the program.'

beats.narration_text: The pipeline lives in one section of that file — the Steps section. Claude reads each step in order and runs it. Linear, no branching unless a step explicitly says otherwise. Here's the design tell: if a step is written there, it runs; if it isn't written, it doesn't exist. The file is the surface area, and Anthropic kept the surface area deliberately small.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR -- three step cards lighting up in order inside a Steps box; a dashed unconnected card sitting apart, outside it

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR -- linear, and only what's written
production_viz.mechanic: A box labelled 'SKILL.md -> Steps' holds three cards -- Step 1, Step 2, Step 3 -- connected left to right by arrows. Each lights up in turn as a read-head passes over it, left to right, strictly in order. THE ANCHOR. Off to the side, outside the box, a fourth card draws in dashed and gray, labelled only '?', unconnected to the arrow chain. It never lights up. A caption lands beneath: 'linear. no branching unless a step says so.' THIS EXACT DASHED CARD RETURNS AT B03.

beats.narration_text: Ask for a step that's actually written in the file, and it runs the same way every time — repeatable, because it's spec, not judgment. Ask for something the file never mentions, and nothing fills the gap. Claude doesn't improvise past the file — the run just ends at the edge of what the file says. That's the trade: they optimized for a boundary you can point at, at the cost of anything you'd want the skill to figure out on its own.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- the three step cards run again in the same order; the dashed card gets an 'ask' arrow and stays dark

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- same steps, and the gap that stays a gap
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 SEQUENCE RETURNS: the same three-card Steps box, the read-head passing over Step 1, 2, 3 in the same order, each lighting teal -- labelled 'same input -> same output'. Beside it, the same dashed '?' card from B02 reappears. An arrow labelled 'ask' points into it. The card does not light; it stays dashed and gray. A line of small italic text appears beneath it: 'not written here. doesn't run.' A final caption at the bottom reads 'spec, not judgment.'

beats.narration_text: closing-checklist runs the steps written in its SKILL.md, the same way every time — not legal judgment, and nothing the file doesn't say.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's a prompt you can paste directly into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini. Tell it you're using an instruction file to run a closing checklist for a transaction, paste in your own draft list of steps, then ask it to execute the list in order — no branching unless a step says so — and to flag anything you ask for that isn't written on the list as 'outside the spec,' so you can see exactly where a spec-driven pipeline ends and your own judgment has to start. Go deeper: for each outside-the-spec item, ask what a new step would have to say, in specific executable language, before the model could handle that item next time without you in the loop.

llm_exercise.prompt: I'm building a closing checklist for a corporate transaction. Here's my draft instruction file that acts as the checklist spec: [paste your list of steps, one per line]. Read it end to end, then walk me through executing it in order, step by step — do not branch or skip unless a step explicitly says to. If I ask you for anything the list doesn't mention, flag it as 'outside the spec' rather than filling it in from your own legal knowledge, and tell me what a new step would have to say, in specific executable language, for the pipeline to cover that item next time.
llm_exercise.dig_deeper: Go deeper: for each item you flagged 'outside the spec,' ask what would have to be written into the file — as a specific, executable step in the same language as the rest of the list — before the model could handle that item next time without your judgment in the loop.
